subject: MAP: Deployment performance roadmap & initial benchmarking outcomes
messages:
From: Sam Wheeler <sam.wheeler@brightloop.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightloop.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking — request + MAP kickoff

Rishi,

Thanks for the call earlier. BrightLoop's procurement team needs a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the evaluation steps and a firm close timeline. The core ask from our side: a side-by-side performance assessment of Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments focused on production characteristics that matter to us — not just peak TPS. We'll want:

- Latency (p50/p95/p99) under typical conversational loads
- Throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec at target prompt sizes)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for interactive experiences
- Concurrency / isolation behavior (how noisy neighbors affect latency)
- Autoscaling behavior and warm-up characteristics
- Determinism and variance over multi-hour runs

Timeline constraints: procurement review on 2026-08-10, commercial terms due 2026-08-17. Can you provide a MAP with concrete milestones and date estimates for test runs, result delivery, and a short in-person demo of the Dedicated footprint?

Attachments: initial_req_brief.pdf (text/plain)

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Wheeler
VP Platform Engineering | BrightLoop Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wheeler <sam.wheeler@brightloop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightloop.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking — MAP & evaluation plan (draft)

Sam — thanks, appreciate the clarity. I put together a draft MAP and an evaluation plan focused on the outcomes you listed. High level: we can complete a two-phase benchmarking engagement ahead of your procurement review if we agree to the outlined scope below.

Quick summary (draft MAP milestones):
- 2026-07-30 to 2026-08-02: Test harness validation + smoke runs (Hosted) — baseline
- 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-05: Dedicated pool tests (steady-state, autoscale/failover)
- 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-07: Private (VPC/on-prem staging) runs — isolation & predictability checks
- 2026-08-08: Consolidated results delivered to BrightLoop (deltas + recommendations)
- 2026-08-09: Executive readout/demo (live) for procurement

Primary deliverables: MAP spreadsheet (milestones + owners), bench_plan_v1.pdf (test configs + data sets), initial_results_summary.csv (raw metrics), short summary slide deck.

Evaluation plan highlights:
- Workloads: 3 canonical prompt templates (chat short/medium/long) with 128–1024 token ranges; mix of open-ended and instruction prompts to capture generation variability.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, requests/sec, error rate, cold-start penalty, tail jitter (std dev).
- Concurrency matrix: runs at [1,4,8,16,32] concurrent sessions depending on deployment capacity.
- Observability: token-level logs, serving traces, and per-request cost estimates.

Notes on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (short):
- Hosted: fastest ramp to test, variable tail under high cross-tenant pressure; autoscale policies are conservative; ideal for quick baseline and smoke tests.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools and controlled isolation; autoscale supports burst windows and we can provision throughput for your SLA.
- Private: maximum isolation and control; depending on on-prem interconnects, you may see best p50/p95 but autoscale behavior is customer-managed and requires orchestration planning.

I've attached bench_plan_v1.pdf and MAP_timeline_v2.xlsx. Marissa will run the harness and Jordan will coordinate Dedicated capacity. Can you confirm access to a representative prompt set and whether we should include any PII in the test data?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wheeler <sam.wheeler@brightloop.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking — harness schedule and early observations

Sam / team — adding a few operational details from the engineering side.

Test harness & data:
- We'll use our standard benchmarking harness (open-source wrapper) tied to a synthetic load generator.
- Please provide a redacted prompt corpus by EOD 7/31. If PII is necessary, we can run in Dedicated only and mark the runs as restricted.

Early smoke results (sanity checks, 7/30 hosted quick run):
- Hosted (shared): p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms at concurrency 4; TTFT ~95ms for short prompts; noticeable variance during baseline noisy windows.
- Dedicated (reserved pool, small test): p50 ~70ms, p95 ~200ms at concurrency 16; stable throughput up to 30 concurrent sessions before queueing grew.
- Private (on-prem staging with NVLink): p50 ~65ms, p95 ~180ms at concurrency 24; no autoscale (manual scale planned), predictability excellent for steady-state but warm-up penalties on cold model load.

Autoscale observations:
- Hosted: reactive scaling with small warm-up penalty; tail latency increases during sudden jumps to 32+ concurrency.
- Dedicated: supports configured burst windows; warm-up largely mitigated by pre-warmed worker pools.
- Private: behaves like Dedicated on steady state but requires pre-provision tooling to achieve similar warm-up characteristics.

I'll run the full matrix on 8/3–8/5 for Dedicated and 8/6–8/7 for Private, with final CSV exported to the shared Drive link in the MAP.

Attachments referenced: initial_results_summary.csv (contains the smoke numbers above plus per-request traces).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Wheeler <sam.wheeler@brightloop.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightloop.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking — harness schedule and early observations

Thanks Rishi/Marissa — that aligns with our expectations. A few clarifying points from procurement/security: 

- Can Dedicated be configured to guarantee a baseline throughput even under noisy neighbors from other internal teams? We need an SLA floor for p95 under committed capacity.
- For Private, is there an optional autoscaling orchestrator you recommend for hybrid on-prem bursting?
- We need SOC2/Audit evidence before the 8/10 procurement review — can you surface the standard package and any region-specific controls (US data residency)?

We'll share the redacted prompt corpus tomorrow. If you can land the MAP timeline and raw CSV by 8/08 EOD, procurement will be able to incorporate the numbers into the cost model.

On the demo: we'd like a short canary of Dedicated topology during the 8/09 readout — a 10–12 minute live run showing steady-state and a controlled scale-up.

Best,
Sam
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wheeler <sam.wheeler@brightloop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightloop.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking — MAP final timeline & next steps

Sam / Olivia / Procurement team — confirmed. Final MAP and deliverables below (attached in Drive and pushed to HubSpot):

Finalized milestones (firm):
- 2026-08-01: Bench harness validation completed (done)
- 2026-08-03: Dedicated capacity full matrix runs complete (Marissa/Jordan owners)
- 2026-08-07: Private runs complete and consolidated exports uploaded
- 2026-08-08 EOD: initial_results_summary.csv + MAP_timeline_v2.xlsx + exec summary slides delivered
- 2026-08-09: 12:00 PM PT — Executive readout + Dedicated canary demo (12-minute steady-state + scale-up sequence)
- 2026-08-12: Procurement follow-up with cost model revisions/DocuSign send

Answers to procurement questions:
- Dedicated SLA floor: yes — we can commit to a p95 SLA on reserved pool sizes with a defined incident credit policy; I'll loop legal after the readout to pin exact numbers in the SOW.
- Private autoscale: we recommend our orchestration add-on (managed autoscaler) for hybrid/private deployments; it integrates with your on-prem scheduler and provides TTL pre-warms for model workers.
- SOC2/Audit evidence: our compliance package (region-specific controls) is attached in the HubSpot deal; I'll have the security team send a short ATO checklist to procurement this afternoon.

Next steps: Marissa will upload the full CSV and per-run traces to the Drive by EOD 8/07. We'll prepare the 12-minute demo script and share a runbook for the canary.

Thanks — looking forward to the readout.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
